abstract: We have designed, fabricated and measured a first generation external modulator for a ~2.4 terahertz quantum cascade laser based on an electrically-driven active terahertz metamaterial structure.

articleTitle: Scaling rules for optimizing 2R regenerators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show through detailed numerical simulations that the ratio of accumulated dispersion to the maximum nonlinear phase shift inside a highly nonlinear fiber can be used to predict the regenerative capability of regenerators making use of fibers with very different lengths, dispersions, and nonlinear parameters.

articleTitle: Multi-core leakage-channel fibers with up to 26000 µm2 combined effective mode-field area
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Hexagonally stacked all-glass multi-core leakage-channel fibers consisting of seven fused silica cores of up to 100µm in diameter were fabricated. Simultaneous fundamental mode propagation in all cores and their active coherent combination was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Ultrafast optical-pump THz-probe spectroscopy of the carrier dynamics in oriented germanium nanowires
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present ultrafast optical-pump THz-probe measurements of the carrier intraband relaxation and interband recombination dynamics in oriented Germanium nanowires. We find 2-3 ps intraband relaxation times and density-dependent recombination times in the 50-100 ps range at 300 K.

Author Keywords: 320.7130 Ultrafast processes in condensed matter, including semiconductors

articleTitle: Solution-cast As2S3 raised strip waveguides for integrated mid-ir optics
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The development of planar chalcogenide glass waveguides leads the way toward integrated mid-infrared optics. As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> waveguides fabricated by solution casting have a transmission loss of 9.47 dB/cm at 4.8 mum.

articleTitle: 10 years of femtosecond combs in Boulder
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Femtosecond combs have been a hot topic in Boulder for the last 10+ years. The first baby steps through the most recent developments will be surveyed.

articleTitle: Sub-50 fs pulse generation from a high power Yb-doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of 48 fs, 226 nJ pulses from an Yb-doped fiber amplifier with 18 W of average power. The system uses a simple stretcher-free, single-stage amplifier configuration. Gain fiber length and pump wavelength are chosen in order to achieve the optimum pulse width and pulse energy.

articleTitle: Optical phase measurements during fs-processing of Materials using time-resolved white-light interferometry
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Fs-laser induced modifications of glasses and metals are investigated in situ by means of time-resolved white-light interferometry. The optical phase shift and corresponding refractive index change is calculated from the interference images.

articleTitle: Large optical springs in picogram-scale optomechanical oscillators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a picogram-scale optomechanical system that increases its mechanical rigidity by more than 5times with the application of mW-level optical power. We discuss the theory and fabrication, making comparisons to existing optomechanical systems.

articleTitle: Dual comb electric field cross-correlation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a novel technique for electric field cross-correlation using two frequency combs. This technique is for characterization of optical arbitrary waveforms and allows independent control of phase and group delay without a mechanical stage.

articleTitle: Phase-stabilized, 1.5-W mid-infrared frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a mid-infrared frequency comb based on a synchronously-pumped, femtosecond optical parametric oscillator. The idler (signal) is continuously tunable from 2.8-4.8 mum (1.76-1.37 mum) with a maximum average output power of 1.50 W.

articleTitle: A tool for designing realizable hyperlenses
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We developed an on-line simulation tool, which facilitates designing experimentally realizable hyperlenses with discrete-layered cylindrical structures. A design working at 340 nm with a resolution of a quarter wavelength is presented.

articleTitle: Distinct dynamic behaviors of high-power photonic-transmitters based on uni-traveling carrier and separated-transport-recombination photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate two high-performance photonic-transmitters based on uni-traveling-carrier-photodiode (UTC-PD) and separated-transport-recombination-photodiode (STR-PD). Thanks to recombination center, STR-PD exhibits comparable maximum-peak-power and electrical pulse-width with much smaller photocurrents and less serious device-heating to those of UTC-PD.

articleTitle: Sensing for autonomous vehicle navigation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This paper introduces GM's research efforts on sensing technologies for autonomous vehicle navigation with an example of a novel LIDAR-based lane-marker detection on GM-CMU's entry Boss, the autonomous vehicle that won the DARPA Urban Challenge.

articleTitle: Coherent population trapping of an electron spin in a single negatively charged quantum dot
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the demonstration of coherent population trapping of an electron spin by means of coherent optical spectroscopy of a single negatively charged quantum dot.

articleTitle: Single-mode Q-switched pulse generation from a tapered DBR laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Q-switching of a 1060 nm quantum-well tapered DBR laser is investigated. Single-mode optical pulses are generated with a peak power of 3.4 W, pulse energy of 1 nJ and a FWHM spectral width of les0.09 nm.

articleTitle: Nonlinear spectral broadening in lead-bismuth-gallate glass photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Highly nonlinear, infrared transmitting lead-bismuth-gallate glass photonic crystal fiber is investigated. Hundred-fold increase in n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> compared to silica and spectral broadening under 1.55 mum ps pumping in 12-cm long PCF are reported.

articleTitle: Miniaturized epi-third harmonic generation microscope with a sub-micron spatial resolution and a video rate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: With a 2D scanning MEMS mirror, we demonstrate a miniaturized epi-third-harmonic-generation microscope with a video rate and a 0.7 mum transverse resolution. In vivo THG imaging of human skin is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Thermo-optic coefficients of monoclinic KLu(WO4)2
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The three thermo-optic coefficients of the biaxial laser host KLu(WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> are measured at 633 nm by a deflection method and nearly athermal propagation directions are found for polarizations along the N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> principal axes.

articleTitle: Near-field correlations in the two-photon field
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate intriguing fine structures in the two-photon field that reflect the (near-field) spatial correlations within the SPDC-generated photon pairs. These structures exhibit among others a surface-enhanced two-photon yield and spatial antibunching.

articleTitle: Nonlinear transfer function in slow light silicon photonic crystal waveguides at 10 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear power transfer function generated through slow-light enhanced nonlinear absorption in silicon photonic crystal waveguides. Pulse regeneration and error reduction in a 10 Gbit/s data signal are observed for 10 MHz amplitude distortion.

articleTitle: Nanophotonic devices for optical networks-on-chip
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe an optical network-on-chip built from passive wavelength routing circuits and tunable micro transmitters based on microdisk sources. Operation of the different subcomponents will be demonstrated.

articleTitle: Spectral hole-burning for solid-state quantum memory
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report progress in using spectral hole-burning in praseodymium doped Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> to prepare an ensemble of Pr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions with a spectral distribution optimized for use in a Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller-type (DLCZ) quantum-repeater scheme.

articleTitle: Phase tunable holographic lithography using a single optical element
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This paper presents the holographic fabrication of three-dimensional photonic crystal templates by forming a five beam interference pattern using a top-cut prism. The interconnecting of the multi-layer structures was controlled by phase-tuning one interfering beam.

articleTitle: Diffusion and redistribution of rubidium in hollow-core photonic bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We characterize the diffusion and redistribution processes that Rb atoms undergo on the inner silica surface of hollow-core photonic bandgap fibers by investigating the dynamics of fiber-transmission and light-induced atomic desorption.

articleTitle: Single photon source for an ion trap quantum network
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Trapped between high numerical aperture laser objectives, a single calcium ion is converted into a high-efficiency source of single photons, with controlled coherence properties. Thereby, various schemes to establish entanglement between remote ions are probed.

articleTitle: Stark effect induced by photogenerated carriers in multiple GaN/AlN asymmetric coupled quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have observed blue and red Stark shifts of two excitonic transition peaks in multiple GaN/AlN asymmetric coupled quantum wells due to increases in electric fields originating from spatial separation of photogenerated electrons and holes.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical transformation of the polarization state with holographic cut cubic crystals
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate very efficient (∼30%) nonlinear optical polarization switch between two linearly cross-polarized states with holographic cut BaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> crystal. The same cut can be used for nonlinear optical transformation of circularly polarized light.

articleTitle: Frequency scanning laser for high speed phase shifting interferometry
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A Multichannel frequency scanning laser which is to be used as a source in a high speed phase-shifting interferometer to measure 3D profiles of nanostructures is presented.

articleTitle: Hypergratings: Sub-diffraction optics with anisotropic plasmonic metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a technique for sub-diffractional focusing in the far field of optical elements. The method combines subwavelength analogs of Fresnel lenses and planar anisotropic metamaterials, used to generate and propagate sub-diffractional information, respectively.

articleTitle: High-power single-frequency thulium-doped fiber master-oscillator power-amplifier at 1943nm
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A Tm-doped fiber master-oscillator power-amplifier system that generates over 100 W of single frequency output in a near-diffraction-limited beam with an M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> parameter of 1.25 is described. The prospects for further increase in power are considered.

articleTitle: Polarizing properties of three-dimensional helical metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the polarizing properties of chiral photonic metamaterials composed of three-dimensional metal helices. The calculated spectra reveal pronounced circular dichroism. Our geometry parameters are compatible with fabrication via direct laser writing and electrodeposition.

articleTitle: Broadcast signal transmission for WDM-PON with ASE injection to an F-P LD
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a novel WDM source for broadcast service using a low-cost Fabry-Perot LD with broadband ASE injection. The proposed optical source provides a cost-effective WDM-PON architecture for broadcast service accommodating more than 32times622 Mb/s.

articleTitle: Vapor Phase Hydrogen Peroxide Imaging Using Photofragmentation Laser-Induced Fluorescence
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Imaging of vapor-phase H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> concentrations is performed using photofragmentation LIF. An Nd:YAG-laser is used for photolysis and a dye laser for LIF on OH generated in the photolysis process. Detection limit is ~30 ppm.

articleTitle: Optical nanofibers for probing cold atoms
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a novel technique for measuring the characteristics of a cloud of cold atoms by monitoring the spontaneous emission coupled into the guided mode of a nanofiber. We show that the fiber is very sensitive to the atoms close to its surface.

articleTitle: Laser gain media based on nanocomposite materials
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We develop simple theoretical models for calculating the gain of layered and Maxwell Garnett composite materials with a resonant component. Laser systems that utilize such composite gain media could display significantly improved properties.

articleTitle: Abstracts
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Presents abstracts of presentations from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Committees
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members.

articleTitle: Citation information
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Citations for papers in these proceedings (or for the proceedings themselves) should follow the examples presented in this document. These examples provide complete information that would be most helpful to a reader or librarian trying to find the proceedings or a paper therein. Some citation styles omit parts of this information.

articleTitle: Agenda of sessions
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: Key to authors and presiders
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Presents an index of the authors whose papers are published in the conference.

articleTitle: Cavity-nano-optomechanics using optical gradient fields
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that evanescent fields of microresonators can be employed for cavity-enhanced high-sensitivity monitoring of nanomechanical motion. This novel scheme opens the path to observing backaction effects using optical gradient forces in the resolved-sideband regime.

articleTitle: Heralded generation of a three-photon NOON state
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A heralded three-photon NOON state is generated from two pairs of photons produced by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC). The measured four-photon coincidences reveal fringes three times finer than single-photon interference.

articleTitle: Optical frequency comb characterization - Self-referenced phase retrieval via spectral shearing interferometry in an A-PPLN waveguide
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A self-referenced technique for measuring the phase of individual optical frequency comb lines is demonstrated. Spectral frequency shear is obtained from sum frequency generation of a signal comb with wavelength separated reference tones.

articleTitle: High sensitivity local evanescent array coupled biosensors with nanometer BSA film
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A LEAC biosensor on a CMOS chip with integrated buried detector array demonstrated 50% photocurrent modulation in response to a patterned nanoscale 2.5 nm thick bovine serum albumin (BSA) film.

articleTitle: Ultra-sensitive Faraday rotation measurements from an atom-light quantum interface
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Highly sensitive Faraday rotation measurements are performed on an ensemble of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb. The deduced interaction strength is discussed in the context of spin squeezing. We present a method for spin state tomography based on Faraday rotation measurements.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of optical wave propagation in PT -symmetric potentials
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Wave propagation in parity-time symmetric potentials is studied for the first time in systems involving a complex refractive index distribution with gain/loss. We demonstrate experimental results for an optically-pumped directional coupler in photorefractive LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>.

articleTitle: Inversion of 3-dimensional polymer photonic crystal fabricated by diffractive optics laser lithography
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Three-dimensional photonic crystal templates fabricated in polymer by single-step laser exposure through a 2D diffractive optical element have been inverted in silica to provide robust structures with strong photonic stopbands in the telecom band.

articleTitle: Ultra-bright narrow-band down-conversion source for atom-photon interaction
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe an ultra-bright source of narrow-band pairs of indistinguishable photons based on cavity-enhanced down-conversion. This source is suitable for experiments on light-matter interactions at the single-photon level.

articleTitle: Liquid crystal spatial light modulator for arbitrary amplitude modulation from ultraviolet to near-infrared
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We fabricated a new liquid-crystal spatial light modulator for amplitude modulation of 315–1100 nm spectrum. Applied voltage and pulse width dependent transmission was characterized, which paves the way for monocycle-pulse shaping and attosecond pulse measurement.

articleTitle: Controlling light propagation via radiation pressure optomechanical coupling
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally for the first time the possibility of controlling the propagation properties of a light pulse using cavity assisted radiation pressure coupling to mechanical modes. Both pulse delay and advancement are experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Mode-locking via active gain modulation in quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A mode-locking mechanism by active gain modulation is studied numerically and experimentally. The parameter window for the emission of stable pulse trains was found. Pulses as short as 3 ps (~0.5 pJ) were characterized by second-order autocorrelation.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg grating sensor for simultaneous measurement of multiple parameters
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an approach to achieve simultaneous measurement of multiple environmental parameters by the use of multiplexed fiber Bragg gratings with coatings of different polymers and specifications on one standard single-mode optical fiber.

articleTitle: Observation of 100 GHz beat signal for millimeter-wave generation using Mach-Zehnder-modulator-based flat comb generator
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We proposed a method for millimeter and terahertz wave generation using a Mach-Zehnder-modulator-based flat comb generator, and showed a 100 GHz beat signal by extracting two modes from 12.5 GHz-spaced comb signals.

articleTitle: Cavity optomechanics with crystalline whispering gallery mode resonators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the optomechanical properties of a high-Q CaF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> whispering gallery mode resonator. Mechanical modes with quality factors up to 135,000 are observed, optically probed and compared to simulation.

articleTitle: Berry phase effect on exciton transport and Bose Einstein condensate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: For excitons in semiconductors, a gauge structure intrinsic to the wavefunction leads to spin-dependent topological transport. When sufficiently large number of excitons have condensed, a nonrotating Bose-Einstein condensate may become unstable against vortex formation.

articleTitle: 270GHz, 580fs optical pulse generation from a single-section quantum-dash Fabry-Pérot laser using frequency multiplication
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Pulse generation from a mode-locked single-section 1.55 mum quantum-dash FP laser is demonstrated under continuous-wave operation. A 270 GHz, 580 fs pulse train is achieved by applying frequency multiplication using fiber dispersion.

articleTitle: Microwave signal mixing in coupled-cavity VCSELs
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Two microwave signals of different frequencies are used to directly modulate the top and bottom cavity of a coupled dual-cavity VCSEL. Signal mixing is observed from the laser output which can be engineered by varying the DC biases to the two cavities.

articleTitle: Characterization and applications of a bright, tunable, MeV class Compton scattering γ-ray source
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report detailed spectral and spatial characterization of a 0.1-MeV-0.8 MeV tunable ultra-bright laser-based Compton scattering source. Nuclear Resonance Fluorescence experiments with the source are also presented.

articleTitle: Frequency noise of a microchip Raman laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report measurement of the fundamental component of frequency noise in a micro-Raman laser fabricated on a silicon chip. A frequency noise spectral component that is equivalent to a Schawlow-Townes linewidth of 3-Hz is measured.

articleTitle: Micro-Air-Bag actuated tunable optofluidic elements
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce for the first time a tuning mechanism for optofluidic devices by embedding a Micro-Air-Bag (MAB) actuator inside a microfluidic chip. Multiple tunable optical elements controlled through the pressure of compressed air were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Room temperature, continuous wave operation of an Sb-based laser grown on GaAs substrate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on the first Sb-based type-I laser grown on GaAs substrate operating continuous-wave around 2.2 mum at room-temperature. The device was grown using solid-source molecular beam epitaxy and comprised two GaInAsSb quantum-wells embedded in AlGaAsSb barriers. Despite the large lattice-mismatch, a good crystalline quality was obtained, and processed devices operated continuous wave up to 50degC, with threshold current densities in the range of 1.5 to 2.2 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. An optical output power of 3.7 mW was obtained at 20degC.

articleTitle: High-Q photonic crystal hetero-slab-edge microcavity laser for index sensing
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We design a photonic crystal hetero-slab-edge microcavity sustaining surface mode with high quality factor ~5.4 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> and index sensitivity of 591 nm/refractive index unit by mode-gap effect. Lasing actions from real devices are also observed.

articleTitle: Spectral and temperature dependence of nonlinear absorption in InSb
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Temperature dependent two-photon and free-carrier absorption spectra of InSb are measured using a tunable picosecond source via temperature controlled Z-scan experiments and show good agreement with theoretical predictions. Three-photon absorption is also observed.

articleTitle: Modulation of uniform light pattern with light extraction enhancement by GaN microlens arrays of LEDs
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The uniform light pattern with light extraction enhancement 250% of LEDs with GaN microlens arrays are demonstrated numerically and experimentally. It makes LED light source as a device of spatial-intensity uniformity integrated with GaN-LEDs structure.

articleTitle: Enhancement in microwave modulation efficiency of vertical cavity surface-emitting laser by optical feedback
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Feedback greatly enhances the high frequency modulation efficiency of VCSELs and provides a means of obtaining high contrast coherent population trapping signals with low rf modulation power.

articleTitle: 1.3-µm wavelength coupled VCSEL arrays employing patterned tunnel junction
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using tunnel junction patterning and double wafer fusion, we demonstrate phase-locked arrays of VCSELs emitting at the 1300 nm waveband. CW powers as high as 10 mW and coherent beams are demonstrated for various array configurations.

articleTitle: Arbitrary radio-frequency waveform generation with a silicon chip-based spectral shaper
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate ultra-compact spectral shaping via thermo-optically tunable multiple-channel microring resonators on a silicon chip, and combine it with frequency-time mapping to achieve photonic radio-frequency arbitrary waveform generation (RFAWG).

articleTitle: Light emission polarization properties of a-plane InGaN/GaN quantum wells light emitting diodes
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the optical characteristics of a nonpolar a-plane InGaN/GaN quantum well (QW) with different indium compositions, QW well widths, and injection carrier densities. We find that the larger indium composition and smaller well width make the energy separation of |Yrang-like state to |Zrang-like state larger, and as a result enhance the polarization ratio of light. However, the polarization ratio decreases as the carrier injection increases, which might be a drawback for high power applications.

articleTitle: Directing optical emission using a Yagi-Uda antenna composed of a finite linear array of gold nanorods
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the realization of a Yagi-Uda antenna array for the optical frequency regime made of gold nanorods. The results suggest that the optical antenna can be used to direct the emission of light.

articleTitle: Simultaneously transfer microwave and optical frequency through fiber using mode-locked fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Microwave and optical frequency references are simultaneously transferred through fiber using a frequency-stabilized mode-locked Er-fiber laser comb. The instability for transferred microwave and optical frequencies are 2.0times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup> and 7.5times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup>@1 s, respectively, for 3 km transmission.

articleTitle: Tunable all-normal-dispersion Yb-doped mode-locked fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Continuous wavelength tunablity is demonstrated in all-normal-dispersion Yb-doped mode-locked fiber laser with a briefringent filter. The mode-locking is self-started and stable. The center wavelength can be tuned from 1024.5 nm to 1070.8 nm.

articleTitle: Aperture-coupled plasmonic ring resonators with submicron bending radii
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose and investigate ultracompact aperture-coupled metallic ring resonators with submicron radii based on strongly-confined plasmonic waveguides. Simulations showed 500nm-radius ring resonators can be obtained with low insertion loss and modal volume of only 0.085(λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Fabrication of intrinsic fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer by imbedding micro air-cavity
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have fabricated an intrinsic fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) by imbedding a micro air-cavity using femtosecond laser and optimal arc-splicing. Spectral analysis confirmed the MZI with experimental results. Temperature dependence was also measured.

articleTitle: High harmonic generation from multiply ionized argon extending beyond 500 eV
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: By combining pulse self-compression and high harmonic generation within a single waveguide, we demonstrate harmonic emission from a multiply ionized gas, extending the cutoff photon energy in Ar to > 500 eV.

articleTitle: Total-internal-reflection-pumped CW Er3+:YAG rod laser with crystalline fiber geometry
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Experimental results on a 1.2 mm diameter 60 mm long, TIR-pumped Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:YAG laser and its thermal lens effects are presented. Up to 9.4 W output power are achieved.

articleTitle: Packet compression from a 10-Gb/s to 270-Gb/s using a temporal telescopic system
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In this paper, a technique is used to temporally compress entire data packets instead of isolated pulses using a temporal imaging system. Experimentally, 24-bit non-return to zero (NRZ) packets at 10 Gb/s is encoded and then temporally compress the packets to a data rate of 270 Gb/s using two optical time-lenses based on four-wave mixing (FWM) in silicon- on-insulator nanowaveguides. This packet compression technique allows for compression of packets using a range of modulation formats and for compression of analog waveforms.

articleTitle: Quantum optical temporal phase estimation by homodyne phase-locked loops
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using classical estimation techniques, we design homodyne phase-locked loops for optical temporal phase and instantaneous frequency measurements at the quantum limit.

articleTitle: Chemical-biological detection overview
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: State-of-the-art sensors and emerging technologies are under development for chemical and biological agent defense. Spectroscopic approaches such as differential scattering, depolarization, and Raman will be discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of O-band polarization entanglement in SMF-28
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of high-quality entangled photon pairs in the 1310-nm O-band. Using an ultra-stable source design, we produce polarization entanglement with 97.5% fidelity as characterized via coincidence basis tomography.

articleTitle: Autofluorescence microscopy for real-time imaging of human esophageal disease
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Autofluorescence microscopy is explored for real-time imaging of human esophagus tissue and detection of disease associated modifications. This approach was also tested using a prototype endoscopy probe.

articleTitle: A bandwidth efficient design of IM/DD optical OFDM
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a new optical OFDM design that achieves significantly improved bandwidth efficiency. We introduce an optimum DC bias to the modulated signal prior to clipping and present an iterative receiver to combat nonlinear distortions.

articleTitle: Active control and spatial mapping of mid-infrared propagating surface plasmons
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Surface waves on metal films with subwavelength features and tunable optical resonances are excited with a quantum cascade laser. The resulting transmission through, and propagation on, the metal/dielectric interface is measured, both spectrally and spatially.

articleTitle: ‘Trapped rainbow’ schemes for storing light in engineered waveguides
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We review recent progress in the realm of ultra-slow and stored light inside metamaterial waveguides. We elucidate a number of critical issues pertaining to the study of light propagation in various slow-light metamaterial structures.

articleTitle: Probing the nonlinear optical response of nanosuspensions
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a fiber-based Z-scan experiment for probing the nonlinear optical response of nanosuspensions that will provide a platform for deciding between rival different theoretical models.

articleTitle: Uniform high bandwidth, high CW power VCSEL arrays
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A high bandwidth, high power, 980 nm vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) array with 3 dB frequency response over 7.5 GHz and continuous wave (CW) power of greater than 120 mW at room temperature is reported.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon polaritons on metal-dielectric nanocomposite films
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate both theoretically and experimentally that the surface plasmon polaritons supported by a metal-dielectric nanocomposite film have properties that fall into one of three distinct categories depending on the metal fill fraction.

articleTitle: Conductivity dynamics in the correlated metallic state of V2O3
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on time resolved studies of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> which is a correlated electron material that undergoes a metal-insulator transition at ~150 K. We observe coherent oscillations in the terahertz conductivity following excitation with 35-fs optical pulses.

articleTitle: Enhancement of magnetic dipole transitions in Lanthanide ions for optical metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present experimental evidence of optically enhanced magnetic dipole transitions from trivalent europium ions. Spectra and lifetime data are used to highlight direct and indirect enhancement pathways, and implications for optical metamaterials are discussed.

articleTitle: Power penalty from amplified spontaneous emission in spatial diversity links
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the power penalty caused by excess amplified spontaneous emission in an optically preamplified receiver for use with a multi-wavelength spatial diversity transmitter to mitigate atmospheric fading.

articleTitle: Macroscopic entanglement between two spatially separated quantum-dot excitons in a planar photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce a formalism for describing the quantum dynamics between two spatially-separated quantum dots on-chip, and apply this formalism to demonstrate pronounced entanglement between two quantum-dot excitons separated by distances of 300 µm and more.

articleTitle: Engineering a telecom-band controlled-NOT gate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We experimentally characterize a linear optics, telecom-band quantum controlled-NOT gate using a fiber-based source of degenerate photon pairs, and bound its process fidelity to 0.907 les Fp les 0.948.

articleTitle: Observation of doubly dressed states in ladder-type electromagnetically induced transparency system
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Doubly dressed states in a ladder-type two-photon, three-level coupling system are observed in our system. The quantum nature of the EIT system significantly suppresses Doppler broadening. The experiments were performed on a room-temperature atomic cesium cell .The cesium atoms are excited by two linearly polarized fields with parallel polarization. The spacing of the EIT doublet is strongly consistent with the theoretical description of the Mollow spectrum, and the numerical simulation demonstrates that Doppler broadening can be greatly reduced using this detection technique.

articleTitle: Ultra-fast quantum dot inversion and switching in a structured electromagnetic vacuum
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel ultra-fast high-contrast switching mechanism of two-level atoms driven by milliwatt picosecond pulse trains in PBG circuits with step-shaped density of states profiles. Possible application as low-threshold, multi-wavelength-channel all-optical transistors is discussed.

articleTitle: Translation of nanoantenna field enhancement by a metal-dielectric composite superlens
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Our simulations show that highly localized field enhancement produced by a periodic array of silver nanoantennas can be translated to the far side of a metal-dielectric composite superlens composed of silver and silica components.

articleTitle: Bi2O3-based Ytterbium doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Ytterbium doped Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-based glasses have been developed. The absorbance is as high as 2600 dB/m/mol. Maximum absorption of 7800 dB/m is achieved. Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-based Ytterbium doped fiber is fabricated, and demonstrated fiber lasers using newly developed fibers.

articleTitle: Large vacuum Rabi splitting in ZnO-based microcavities
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the growth and characterization of bulk ZnO-based hybrid microcavity (MC). The phenomenon of strong exciton-photon coupling at room temperature has been observed in the ZnO-based MC. The cavity quality factor is 221. The experimental results show good agreement with calculated exciton-polariton dispersion curves based on transfer matrix method. From the theoretical and experimental exciton-polariton dispersion curves with two different cavity-exciton detuning values, the large vacuum Rabi splitting is estimated to be 58 meV in the ZnO-based MC.

articleTitle: A trapped-ion phonon laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A cooled, trapped Mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ion is excited using a continuous, blue-detuned pump. Coherent oscillatory motion is observed. It is shown to result from stimulated emission of center-of-mass phonons, constituting the mechanical analog of a laser.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband near-IR non-collinear optical parametric amplification in potassium niobate and lithium niobate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on generation of ultra-broadband (>2900 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) near-IR pulses from non-collinear optical parametric amplifier based on congruent lithium niobate and potassium niobate bulk crystals pumped at 800 nm.

articleTitle: Non-traditional cyanines: Candidate materials for all-optical signal processing applications
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Development of non-traditional cyanine systems has allowed for improvements in the material properties required for all-optical signal processing applications: enhanced third-order nonlinearity, low nonlinear losses, improved processability, and controlled intermolecular interactions in the solid-state.

articleTitle: Plasmonic sensors based on semiconductor laser diode packages
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We combine Plasmonic grating structures with commercially available semiconductor laser diode packages to realize a prototype miniaturized chemical/bio-sensor.

articleTitle: The Dirac point of photonic graphene
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Photonic graphene is an optical analogue to electronic graphene. We introduce Dirac maps to design a structure of alumina rods and experimentally demonstrate the existence of an Dirac point at 17 GHz in transmission measurements.

articleTitle: Light-induced reversible shift and control of the bandgap of bulk CdZnTe:V crystals
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the experimental observation of very large, light-induced, reversible change in the bandgap (up to 70 meV) of CdZnTe:V crystals. Above a specific threshold, the bandgap shift persists when illumination is turned off.

articleTitle: Real time ammonia detection in exhaled human breath with a quantum cascade laser based sensor
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Quantum cascade laser based breath sensor platform for medical applications employing a quartz-enhanced photoacoustic spectroscopy technique is reported. The detection sensitivity for exhaled ammonia is at <10 ppbv level with 1 s time resolution.

articleTitle: Ultrafast all-optical switching with a single quantum dot
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical switching based on a single quantum dot coupled to a photonic crystal cavity. The quantum-dot mediated interaction between the signal and control beams occurs at the single-photon level.

articleTitle: Optical interferometers with reduced sensitivity to thermal noise
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Thermal phase noise in optical interferometry can be compensated by exploiting coherence for underlying stochastic displacements and strains. The phase upon reflection from a fluctuating mirror's surface can thereby have reduced sensitivity to thermal noise.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Ytterbium doped INNOSLAB amplifier with high average power
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A diode-pumped ytterbium doped INNOSLAB fs-amplifier with 400 W output power was realized. The pulse duration of the output pulses was almost transform limited 682 fs for Yb:YAG at a pulse repetition rate of 76 MHz. This was achieved at room temperature without the use of any stretcher or compressor setup.

articleTitle: A high-power passively Q-switched monolithic solid-state laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A passively Q-switched monolithic solid-state laser with a crystal of Nd:YAG+Cr:YAG bonded at room temperature and a fiber-coupled LD stack was developed. 12 mJ output with 50 Hz and 2.3 ns pulse width was achieved.

articleTitle: Imaging with ultrashort shaped pulses
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Ultrashort shaped pulses are becoming available and their use for biomedical imaging will permit signal enhancements, allow selective excitation, and reduced photobleaching. These pulses are also enabling new imaging modalities which provide greater chemical information.

articleTitle: Widely tunable, phase-locked CW-THz radiation by photomixing of two CW lasers locked to two independent fiber combs
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Arbitrary single-frequency CW-THz-wave generator based on two-independent femtosecond fiber-combs is presented. Continuous tuning of a 120-GHz CW wave was demonstrated across several MHz, which is limited by electric bandwidth of THz- for evaluation.

articleTitle: High power injectorless quantum cascade laser structure in the 6.0 µm wavelength range
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An injectorless quantum cascade laser design, using two 0.6 nm InAs spikes within the active zone, yielding shorter wavelength and improved performance is presented. The average pulsed output power was measured to 880 mW at 297 K.

articleTitle: Silicon avlanche photodiodes for low cost, high loss short wavelength radio over fiber links
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An APD is shown to improve the noise figure of a lossy optical link compared to a PIN-TIA combination of equivalent gain. Transmission of IEEE 802.11g WLAN signals is demonstrated with 18 dB optical link loss.

articleTitle: Near-infrared fluorescent labeling of tissue transglutaminase substrates for wound healing monitoring
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel imaging strategy is developed to optically monitor the wound healing process by crosslinking near-infrared fluorescent-labeled tissue transglutaminase substrates into the wound.

articleTitle: Generation of a 1 picosecond soft x-ray laser pulses from an injection-seeded plasma amplifier
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Phase-coherent soft x-ray laser pulses of 1.13 plusmn 0.47 ps duration were generated by injection-seeding a solid-target Ne-like Ti plasma amplifier with high harmonic pulses. This is the shortest pulse duration reported to date from a table-top soft x-ray laser amplifier.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser frequency comb for precision astrophysical spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: High-resolution spectroscopy is a crucial tool for cosmology and the search for extrasolar planets. We present a laser comb with up to 40-GHz line spacing for use as a new spectrographic calibration source.

articleTitle: IR index sensing based on surface phonon-polaritons in SiC
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present results demonstrating the excitation of surface phonon-polaritons at the interface between SiC and different materials. The resonant nature of the excitation can be used to sense minute substance amounts or distinguish between substances.

articleTitle: High-power GaN-based blue-violet laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have succsessfully developed blue-violet laser diodes having the world's highest output power of 450 mW by introducing a novel facet coating structure, reducing the internal loss in devices, and making a cavity length long.

articleTitle: MINIATOM: Miniaturized coherent atom sensors
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We conceive and build a compact cold atom interferometer with an original architecture based on integrated optical components. These new inertial sensors can play a significant role in navigation, fundamental physics and earth observation.

articleTitle: Nanorod light emitting diode arrays with highly concentrated radiation profile and strain relaxed structure
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have developed a natural lithography method to fabricate nanorod structure. The spin-on glass is used as a space layer to realize the nanorod LED. The strain is released in nanorod structured LED which is indicated by their nearly constant electroluminescent peak wavelength at the injection current range between 25mA and 100mA. Furthermore, a highly concentrated radiation profile is observed from the nanorod LED array. We suggest a light guided concept to explain the narrow radiation phenomena.

articleTitle: Portable spectroscopic carbon dioxide monitor for carbon sequestration applications
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A portable sensor for CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> monitoring based on quartz enhanced photoacoustic spectroscopy (QEPAS) technology and using a DFB diode laser operating at lambda = 1.57 mum will be described. The sensor is primarily intended for studies of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> penetration through soil.

articleTitle: Cavity quantum electrodynamics in electrically driven quantum dot-micropillar cavities
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on cavity quantum electrodynamics effects in high-Q electrically contacted quantum dot-micropillar cavities. The structures show weak coupling and strong coupling via electrooptical tuning as well as single photon emission and low threshold lasing.

articleTitle: Four-well highly strained Quantum Cascade Lasers grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel four-well injectorless design with short wavelength (5.5 mum) and room temperature operation utilizing highly strained Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.35</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.65</sub>As/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.70</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.30</sub>As (0.8/-1.5%) quantum wells.

articleTitle: Study of four-wave mixing between a coherent signal and incoherent pump in a highly-nonlinear fiber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Four-wave mixing between a coherent laser signal and incoherent pump in highly nonlinear fiber are investigated theoretically and experimentally, and the effect of incoherence pump on signal is studied.

articleTitle: Intense multi-μJ high-order harmonics generated from neutral atoms of In2O3 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study high-order harmonic generation in plasma containing an abundance of indium oxide nanoparticles. We find that harmonics from nanoparticles are intense, with high-order harmonic energy ranging from 6 muJ for the 9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic to 1 muJ for the 17<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic. However, the harmonic cut-off is at the 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order, which is much lower than that observed using solid indium oxide targets. By comparing the harmonic spectrum obtained using solid and nanoparticle indium oxide, we conclude that the intense harmonics from nanoparticles are generated from neutral atoms.

articleTitle: Self-adaptive common-path Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography with real-time surface recognition and feedback control
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a self-adaptive common-path Fourier-domain OCT system with real-time surface recognition and feedback control. The scanning probe tracks the sample surface variance and effective imaging depth was largely extended to the probe's free-moving range.

articleTitle: Growths of staggered InGaN quantum wells light-emitting diodes emitting at 520–525 nm employing graded-temperature profile
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The use of 3-layer staggered InGaN quantum wells light-emitting diodes at 520–525 nm, grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition with graded-temperature profile, resulted in increase in efficiency and output power by 2-times.

articleTitle: Double photonic bandgap hollow-core PCF
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on the design, fabrication and characterization of hollow-core photonic crystal fiber with two robust bandgaps that bridge the benchmark laser wavelengths 1064 nm with 1550 nm, and 1064 nm with 780 nm.

articleTitle: Real-time coherent imaging of ultrafast ablation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: By integrating coherent imaging (optical coherence tomography) into an ultrafast machining platform, we directly monitor surface and subsurface changes in sample morphology due to the laser ablation and subsequent relaxation between laser pulses.

articleTitle: Fiber-laser-pumped CW OPO for red, green, blue laser generation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report a cw-RGB laser based on an Yb-fiber-laser pumped OPO with intra- and extracavity wavelength converters. At 25-W pump power, the laser generated 5, 0.5, and 0.01-W at 633, 532, and 450 nm, respectively.

articleTitle: Funneling of terahertz electromagnetic waves through nanogap device
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that terahertz waves transmit through a lambda/30,000 nanogap separating two conducting planes. The field enhancement responsible for the light funneling has a 1/f dependence, which originates from the charging time of the gap.

articleTitle: Emission characteristics of 2D photonic crystal band edge organic blue lasers designed at three surface-emitting emission band edges
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In this paper, two-dimensional photonic crystal band-edge lasers of triangular lattice is designed based on photonic band diagrams and the organic material PTT acts as the gain media. The gain medium consists of a small molecule blue emitting dye 2-(4-(pyren-l-yl)phe-nyl)triphenylene (PTT) doped in poly(N-vinylcarbazole) PVK. The emission characteristics are presented. The lasing phenomenon is occurred only at MII point (emission band locations).

articleTitle: Generation of Sub-20fs ultraviolet pulses with achromatic phase-matching sum frequency mixing
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: 17.4 fs ultraviolet pulses with 400 nJ energy were generated by sum frequency mixing of 805 nm pulses and ultra-broadband visible pulses. Angular dispersion was introduced to achieve broadband phase-matching.

articleTitle: Colorless, surface normal optical modulator based on free carrier effect in gallium arsenide
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a surface-normal modulator based on free-carrier effect in GaAs and phase-to-amplitude conversion coupling to a single mode fiber. Operation over 1200-2400 nm, modulation depth up to 43% and frequency up to 270 MHz is observed.

articleTitle: Generation of continuous mode-locked pulses in Nd:YVO4 with an adjustable pulse duration between 34 ps and 1 ns
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on highly stable active continuous mode-locking in diode-pumped Nd:YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> with adjustable pulse durations between 34 ps and 1 ns. An average output power till 7.3 W, an excellent beam quality M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><.1 and transform-limited pulses were obtained.

articleTitle: Optical tweezers with optically resonant particles
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Optical tweezers are typically used on transparent dielectric particles. Particles with optical resonances should experience a larger trapping force near resonance. We present a numerical and experimental study of trapping force on such particles.

articleTitle: Quantum state preparation with waveguides and photon counting
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Recent progress in quantum communication highlights the need of advanced non-Gaussian states exhibiting high purity and spatio-spectral single-mode characteristics. We employ tailored waveguides and photon counting to implement efficient state preparation suitable for quantum networks.

articleTitle: Scattering-probe-imaging of the field confinement on tapered metal-wire waveguides
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using a recently developed scattering-probe-imaging technique, we observe strong confinement of the THz electric field at the end of a tapered metal-wire waveguide compared to an un-tapered wire. This confinement agrees well with FEM simulations.

articleTitle: Mode-selective single-beam Coherent anti-Stokes Raman Scattering spectroscopy of gas phase molecules
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Binary phase shaping is applied to single-beam CARS spectroscopy of gas mixtures, such as ambient air, and is shown to provide mode-selectivity and enhanced non-resonant background suppression capability when compared with the original technique.

articleTitle: Negative permeability using arrays of aperiodic silver nanoclusters
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a metamaterial architecture that exhibits a strong magnetic resonance leading to negative effective permeability. The building blocks are aperiodic silver nanowire clusters that generate stronger magnetic resonance than their periodic counterparts.

articleTitle: Optofluidically tunable MMI filter
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An optofluidically tunable multimode interference (MMI) bandpass filter is demonstrated. This scheme allows for a tuning range of almost 40 nm, by simple changing the liquid refractive index around the multimode fiber of the filter.

articleTitle: Low-power and fast switching in III–V photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on recent advancements in membrane photonic crystals based on III-V semiconductors. We fabricated highly nonlinear waveguides with low insertion losses and demonstrate ultra-fast all-optical response to ultra-low energy excitation in resonant cavities.

articleTitle: Experimental confirmation of a generalized definition of the effective nonlinear coefficient in emerging waveguides with subwavelength structures
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A new vectorially-based definition of effective nonlinear coefficient λ is presented and its validity is confirmed experimentally using a bismuth suspended-core fiber with the core diameter of 530 nm and measured λ of 5400±200 W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>.

articleTitle: How filament-induced birefringence affects the THz generation from the filament in air
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A femtosecond laser filament can induce birefringence in an isotropic medium. This birefringence leads to the generation of elliptically polarized THz pulses emitting from a single-color/two-color filament in air.

articleTitle: Multiple chemical sensor using a rapidly tuned external cavity quantum cascade laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous detection of multiple airborne chemicals at low-ppb concentrations using a sensor based on a rapid tuning of an external cavity quantum cascade laser from 7.87-8.70 mum.

articleTitle: Ultrafast switching of light into surface plasmons: an active grating coupler
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Near-infrared pump/visible probe measurements on gold gratings demonstrate picosecond control of grating assisted coupling to surface plasmon polaritons. On-off switching ratios as large as 5.3 dB are possible.

articleTitle: High quality factor photonic crystal nanocavities in “impossible scenarios”: Dual-polarization, low-index materials and air-band modes
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We for the first time present designs of high-Q photonic crystal nanocavities in the cases previously rendered “impossible”, including an ultra-high Q dual-polarized nanocavities, high Q/V cavities based on low-index materials, and high-Q air-band-mode cavities.

articleTitle: Fast characterization of optical arbitrary waveforms from a 10GHz frequency comb using dual-quadrature spectral interferometry
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate fast (~1.4 mus) spectral amplitude and phase characterization of optical arbitrary waveforms generated by line-by-line shaping of a 10 GHz frequency comb. Our technique enables coherent spectral phase measurement after dispersive propagation over long (~50 km) lengths of optical fiber.

articleTitle: Correlation spectroscopy of third-harmonic generation by single nanorods
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have observed third-harmonic generation by single nanorods in solution and investigated its excitation polarization dependence. Our findings demonstrate the possibility of using third-harmonic signals for correlation spectroscopy, in contrast to conventional fluorescence correlation spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Area theorem and energy quantization for dissipative optical solitons
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We derive a dissipative soliton area theorem that contrasts with other area theorems: the energy scales directly with the pulse duration, and the energy has an upper bound. Predictions are verified in a fiber oscillator.

articleTitle: Spin-Polarized Electron Transport in GaAs: Role of Holes
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Spin-polarized electron transport in GaAs is studied with emphasis on the role of holes. Sub-picosecond ac spin current pulses are produced and ambipolar spin diffusion are studied, both dominated by space charge field of holes.

articleTitle: New concepts for depth resolved holographic imaging based on spectrally tunable diode lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present two new depth resolved holographic imaging concepts with spectrally tunable diode lasers. Variable depth resolution is achieved by changing the tuning width and a concept for single-shot recording of a 3D-image is introduced.

articleTitle: Low divergence, single-lobed, surface emission from THz photonic-crystal quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate full control of the spectral and spatial emission properties of terahertz quantum cascade lasers using metallic photonic-crystals for lateral confinement. Single-mode, surface-emission is obtained at a frequency of 2.8-2.9 THz using a photonic-crystal design with a square lattice geometry. The resonator quality factor is then optimised, using a graded photonic-crystal architecture, and this leads to an increased maximum operating temperature of 151 K. Furthermore, the introduction of a carefully designed pi-shift yields single-lobed surface emission (~12deg times 8deg), with a peak output power of 5 mW at 78 K.

articleTitle: Vibrational coherence modulated interfacial third harmonic generation spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a new interfacial probing technique of vibrational spectroscopy to provide additional insight over current methods on the structure and dynamics of interfacial boundaries.

articleTitle: Exciton-exciton annihilation in organic polariton microcavities
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Sublinear intensity dependence of photoluminescence from organic exciton-polariton microcavities under non-resonant excitation in two power regimes is shown. The sublinearity is attributed to exciton-exciton annihilation, which could compete with polariton-polariton scattering in these devices.

articleTitle: Efficient generation of a coherent water window x-ray by phase-matched high-order harmonic
