abstract: We report break-up of cylindrical shell into well-ordered filament arrays by optical-fiber thermal drawing. Enhanced photosensitivity of centimeter-long crystalline-Se nano-filaments is observed and the mechanism is discussed. This work paves a way to in-fiber nanodevices.

articleTitle: Ultrafast re-routing of slow light in a nanophotonic directional coupler
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that we can switch the transmission of a directional coupler from one output port to another within a time as short as 3 ps with laser pulse energies of less than 10 pJ.

articleTitle: 1.27 W, tunable, continuous-wave, single-frequency, solid-state blue source
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a tunable, cw, single-frequency blue source based on internal SHG of a cw singly-resonant OPO, providing up to 1.27 W across 425-489 nm with a passive frequency stability <280 MHz over >5 minutes.

articleTitle: Table-top soft x-ray microscope adopting a PMMA phase-reversal zone plate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A table-top soft X-ray microscope, adopting a phase-reversal zone plate (PRZP) made of PMMA and high harmonic x-ray source, was constructed. The PMMA PRZP showed enhanced imaging efficiency compared to a metallic Fresnel zone plate.

articleTitle: Eye-safe Pr3+:RbPb2Cl5 Laser at ∼1.65 µm resonantly-pumped at 1547 nm
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Resonantly-pumped laser action based on <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> rArr <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> transition of Pr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ion is reported for the first time. Pr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:RbPb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> laser demonstrated slope efficiency of over 21% at 1647 nm despite the marginal initial sample quality.

articleTitle: Contrast challenge for ultrahigh-intensity experiments on high-density targets
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Current contrast-control-technology is inadequate for solid targets with the next generation of high-intensity lasers. We apply a spatiotemporal-contrast-concept (STC) to demonstrate that intensity ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is feasible for transparent solids at STC ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>.

articleTitle: 1.3µm electroabsorption modulator with InAs/InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electroabsorption properties of 1.3mum InAs/InGaAs/GaAs quantum dot electroabsorption modulator (EAM) are investigated. Onset of absorption to higher electric field suggests the potential to achieve higher optical power handling capability than conventional EAM.

articleTitle: Image-guided Raman endoscopy for in vivo detection of high grade dysplasia in gastric
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the feasibility of near infrared (NIR) Raman spectroscopy coupled with narrow band imaging for distinguishing high grade dysplasia from normal gastric mucosa tissues at gastroscopy.

articleTitle: Quantum diffraction of biphoton beam at a blazed grating
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A blazed grating is used for the separation of single photons from photon pairs. The Fraunhofer far field of the two-photon rate depends on the spatial correlation strength of the photons and enables correlation characterizations.

articleTitle: Conversion efficiency, scaling and global optimization of high harmonic generation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Closed form expressions for the high harmonic generation (HHG) conversion efficiency in the plateau and cut-off region are derived showing agreement with previous observations. Application of these results to optimal HHG-based-XUV-sources is discussed.

articleTitle: A compact wideband flat-band filter for silicon photonic applications
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A compact coupled-resonators flat-band filter with a large bandwidth (~3.3 nm), large free-spectral range (~18 nm), low crosstalk (<-12 dB) and negligible insertion loss (<0.5 dB) is demonstrated on a silicon-on-insulator platform with focused applications for on-chip optical interconnects.

articleTitle: Fiber laser with enhanced modelocking using a carbon nanotube-filled micro-Slot saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a robust, compact, low-loss saturable absorber consisting of a liquid core waveguide, engraved in an optical fiber and filled with carbon nanotubes. Enhanced modelocking in an all-fiber configuration is achieved.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon polariton enhanced fluorescence from quantum dots on nanostructured metal surfaces
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Surface-plasmon-polariton-enhanced fluorescence from CdSe/ZnS quantum dots (QD) deposited onto patterned gold/PMMA substrates has been observed, and the enhancement related to QD position with regard to the type of surface and nanostructures.

articleTitle: Direct comparison of absolute distance meter using an optical comb and integrated optical interferometer with an optical sub-wavelength accuracy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Distance measurements using the 821<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>-harmonic of the intermode beat frequency in an optical comb with optical-sub-wavelength accuracy are demonstrated. Direct comparison with a laser interferometer for the same optical setup reveals good agreement to 20-nm.

articleTitle: Atomic physics and quantum information processing with superconducting circuits
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Superconducting circuits using Josephson junctions can behave like atoms making transitions between discrete energy levels. Such circuits can test quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales and be used to conduct atomic-physics experiments on a silicon chip.

articleTitle: Design of suspended AlGaAs waveguides for tunable difference frequency generation in mid-IR
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A birefringent phase-matching scheme for difference frequency generation in a slotted air-clad waveguide with tunable gap width is proposed and theoretically analyzed. Tunability of 300 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and efficiency of 200 W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> is predicted.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser-induced periodic surface structures on tungsten
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We generate periodic surface structures on tungsten at various laser wavelengths, despite that the table values of the dielectric constants indicate the absence of surface plasmons, a wave necessary for forming periodic structures on metals.

articleTitle: Application of UV LEDs to the design of low cost biological aerosol detectors
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Measuring UV-excited fluorescence from individual airborne particles is a leading technique for fast, non-specific detection of biological threat aerosols. UV-LEDs, available at several wavelengths, enable cost reduction of these detectors while presenting additional design challenges.

articleTitle: Extremely simple device for measuring ultrashort pulses in the visible
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an extremely simple frequency-resolved-optical-gating device (GRENOUILLE) ideal for measuring visible ultrashort pulses. By angle-tuning a thick crystal, its range includes almost the entire visible spectrum.

articleTitle: Frequency swapping using an optical switch with embedded Mach-Zehnder structures for wavelength-converted optical signal routing without lightsources
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We proposed and experimentally investigated a frequency swapping technique for two lightwaves by using a LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> optical switch where only Mach-Zehnder structures were nested. 10-GHz opposite frequency shifts for two lightwaves were successfully obtained.

Author Keywords: (060.1810) Buffers, couplers, routers, switches, and multiplexers

articleTitle: Fabrication of gold-platinum nanoparticles by intense, femtosecond laser irradiation of aqueous solution
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated fabrication of gold and platinum composite and/or alloy nanoparticles by intense, femtosecond pulsed laser irradiation of mixed auric and platinum aqueous solution.

articleTitle: Elliptically polarized high harmonic emission from molecules driven by linearly polarized light
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We perform an accurate polarimetry measurement of high harmonic emission from aligned molecules. Surprisingly, we find that harmonic emission from N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecules can be strongly elliptically polarized even when driven by linearly polarized laser fields.

articleTitle: Efficient carrier envelope offset locking for a frequency comb by modifying a collinear f-to-2f interferometer
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a carrier-envelope-offset-locked frequency comb with 500-pJ pulse energy, with increased coupling efficiency into a tellurite PCF by using angled-V-groove splicing. Carrier-envelope-offset stabilization at telecommunications wavelengths is achieved at the lowest pulse energy.

articleTitle: High repetition rate optical parametric amplification based on a single Yb:fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: 700-1900-nm tunable single-pass optical-parametric-amplification was demonstrated. The pump was a frequency-doubled Yb-laser, and the residual Yb-laser was recycled to generate supercontinuum as seeding. Over 30% conversion efficiency was obtained with 10-nJ pump energy.

articleTitle: Raman fiber laser arrays
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose and analyze coupled fiber lasers based on Raman gain. The nonlinear phases inherent in the stimulated Raman scattering process are shown to contribute to the phase locking mechanism in the weak coupling regime.

articleTitle: Cavity-QED assisted “attraction” between an exciton and a cavity mode in a planar photonic-crystal cavity
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce a new regime of light-matter interaction, whereby a single exciton and photonic-crystal cavity mode are mutually ldquoattractedrdquo as they are tuned through resonance. This phenomenon is successfully explained by a quantized medium-dependent theory.

articleTitle: Ultra precise frequency dissemination across Germany - Towards a 900 km optical fiber link from PTB to MPQ
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In order to compare optical frequency standards over large distances PTB and MPQ are establishing an optical fiber link of more than 900 km length. We report the intermediate results of this project.

articleTitle: Terahertz generation and detection using frequency conversion
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Terahertz is nonlinearly upconverted to telecommunication wavelengths, resulting in detection with 4.5 pW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> noise equivalent power and nanosecond temporal resolution. Optical frequencies from an ultrashort pulse mix, generating 3 mW of broadband terahertz.

articleTitle: Ultrafast all-optical modulation in GaAs photonic crystal cavities
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical modulation via ultrafast optical carrier injection in a GaAs photonic crystal cavity using a degenerate pump-probe technique. The low switching(absorption) energy~120 fJ(10 fJ), and fast response(~15 ps), limited only by carrier lifetime, suggest practical all-optical switching applications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Terahertz Spectroscopy of Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Studies are presented that combine optical and THz excitation in the linear and nonlinear regimes. The analysis focuses on exciton formation and decay, the plasmonic response, THz gain, excitonic Rabi flopping, and quantum-state control.

articleTitle: Impedance-matching surface plasmon absorber for FDTD siumulation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The perfectly matched layer (PML) is used to be excellent boundary in the finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD), but is failure to absorb surface plasmon (SP) directly. In order to absorbing the incident SP at the end on a metal surface, an impedance-matching layer (IML) is implemented between scattered SP and PML. A very low SP reflection of -28.69 dB is achieved by an IML with length of lambda/3. The IML significantly reduces the reflected SP without significantly increasing the simulation area and creates a quasi-infinite regime for SP propagation.

articleTitle: Designing high-speed, low-chirp, low-distortion microring modulators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that microring modulators with variable coupling strengths can have low distortion, zero chirp, high extinction ratios, and large modulation rates only limited by the coupler or the free spectral range of the resonator.

articleTitle: 2.5 Gbps Electro-optic modulator in deposited silicon
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate GHz-speed electro-optic modulation using microring resonators in a deposited layer of polycrystalline silicon. Active optical devices in a deposited microelectronic material can enable monolithic large-scale integration of photonic networks on a microelectronic chip.

articleTitle: Studies on the relative advantages of quantum-dot and quantum-well gain media in lasers and amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The merit of quantum-dot versus quantum-well lasers is much debated. This paper describes an attempt at an answer by examining intrinsic behavior and underlying physics, using a microscopic theory with a rigorous treatment of scattering.

articleTitle: Quantum optics in laser-written waveguide circuits
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Building quantum optical circuits with waveguides-on-a-chip networks is a practical route to scalable quantum information processing. We report circuits made using direct-write laser techniques that create high fidelity, 2 or 3-dimensional, fiber compatible quantum networks.

articleTitle: Impulsive alignment of N2 with a train of 8 pulses
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a scheme that exploits the time periodicity of rigid rotors by breaking a single strong alignment pulse into an eight pulse train. Our results show langcos<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> thetasrang > 0.6 in nitrogen gas at 1 ATM and 300 K.

articleTitle: Synchronously pumped OPO with two pulses per cavity for intracavity phase measurements
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Phase to frequency conversion is demonstrated with a synchronously modelocked optical parametric oscillator, with a sensitivity of 16 MHz/radian, and a phase resolution of 9ldr10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> radian.

articleTitle: Near infrared silicon quantum dots MOSFET detector
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Fully Si-based MOSFET photodetector was demonstrated at optical telecommunication wavelengths by using a gate dielectric stack comprising of a Si quantum dots film. Illumination at wavelengths lambda=1.55 mum, photoresponse as high as 2.0 A/W was measured.

articleTitle: Failure mode investigation of high power multi-mode InGaAs-AlGaAs strained quantum well lasers using time-resolved EL and EBIC techniques
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report our failure mode investigation of high power multi-mode InGaAs-AlGaAs strained quantum well (QW) lasers using time-resolved electroluminescence (EL) and electron beam induced current (EBIC) techniques.

articleTitle: Measuring photon direction in high-index-contrast waveguides
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that within high-index-contrast waveguides, photons traveling in different directions can follow slightly different trajectories. Using near-field microscopy we distinguish between forward and backward propagating photons.

articleTitle: Surface emitting photonic crystal mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate spectrally single-mode, low-divergence surface-emission from photonic-crystal quantum cascade lasers operating in the mid-infrared spectral range (λ∼7.2µm). The photonic-crystal resonator is defined by the sole top metallization. No semiconductor etch is employed. The effective index contrast is induced by the different profiles of surface plasmon and air-confined modes. Numerical electromagnetic simulations show that the resonator Q-factor depends strongly on the r/a ratio. The devices - which operate up to 220 K - exhibit single mode emission with a side mode suppression ratio ≥20/25dB. The far-field emission pattern is doughnut-shaped, with a full divergence angle of ∼12 degrees.

articleTitle: Observation of an optical Feshbach resonance in 88Sr
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have tuned the s-wave scattering length of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</sup>Sr via an optical Feshbach resonance. Change in the rate of thermalization of atoms reveals a slight increase in the phase space density of the atom sample.

articleTitle: Passively generated high repetition rate pulse bursts using a fiber laser with a polarization maintaining section
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Pulse bursts of sub-THz rates are passively generated in a mode locked fiber laser. Repetition rates are controlled by the differential group delay of an intra cavity polarization maintaining fiber. Simulations and experiments are reported.

articleTitle: Mechanism of the multiple Raman sidebands generation in diamond pumped by two femtosecond pulses
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Detailed angle resolved spectroscopy reveals that intense multiple Raman-Nath like CARS signals (350-720 nm) are generated in diamond under pumping of two-phonon Raman peak by two-color femtosecond pulses.

articleTitle: Multi-wavelength sensing of greenhouse gases by rapidly swept continuous-wave cavity ringdown spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The greenhouse gas molecules CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O are detected by using a cavity ringdown laser spectrometer with rapidly swept optical cavity and multi-wavelength coherent radiation. This sensitive portable instrument is applicable to environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Highly multiplexed antibody-antigen detection using nanoscale optofluidic resonators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a highly multiplexable optofluidic biosensor consisting of arrays of evanescently coupled photonic crystal resonators. We show the ability to monitor binding kinetics of Anti-Streptavidin in real-time and investigate the limit-of-detection (LOD) of the sensor.

articleTitle: Quantum information processing with double-well optical lattices
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a technique to address a spatially dense field-insensitive qubit register composed of neutral atoms held in a double-well optical lattice. We robustly perform single-qubit rotation on qubits located at addressed lattice sites.

articleTitle: Nonlinear generation and manipulation of Airy beams
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a quadratic nonlinear photonic structure that converts a fundamental Gaussian beam to an accelerating Airy beam at the second harmonic. The nonlinear response enables all-optical switching of the beam's acceleration direction.

articleTitle: Light localization and label-free colorimetric sensing with deterministic aperiodic photonic structures
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We theoretically investigate light localization and local density of states manipulation in aperiodic photonic structures and discuss their applications as pseudo-random lasers and label-free optical biosensors.

articleTitle: Two-photon interference for quantum cryptography with a non-maximally entangled photon pair
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel scheme of quantum cryptography with the two-photon interference of a non-maximally entangled photon pair. The security is based on the impossibility of the local unitary transformation between the certain non-maximally entangled states.

articleTitle: Characteristics of carbon nanotube saturable absorbers for solid-state laser mode-locking near 1.25 µm
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Different types of carbon nanotube saturable absorbers were fabricated and characterized. Their application for solid-state laser mode-locking enabled the generation of sub-100-fs pulses near 1.25 mum with powers up to 280 mW at 79 MHz.

articleTitle: XUV supercontinua supporting pulse durations of sub-one atomic unit of time
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Double optical gated high-order harmonic supercontinuous spectra were generated in the extreme ultraviolet region including the “water window”. The spectra supported 16 as pulse durations that are below one atomic unit of time (24 as).

articleTitle: Two-cycle light pulses in the near and mid infrared by PPSLT-based optical parametric amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present two ultrabroadband optical parametric amplifiers based on periodically poled stoichiometric lithium tantalate. Both systems produce two-cycle pulses, in the near-infrared (8.5 fs at 1.3 mum) and mid-infrared (25 fs at 3.5 mum) respectively.

articleTitle: Cavity optomechanics
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Cavity enhancement of optical fields is providing a new way to couple light and mechanical motion. Its application to mechanical cooling and amplification, example implementations, and prospects for new science and technology are reviewed.

articleTitle: Direct observation of the conical intersection in cis-trans photoisomerization of rhodopsin
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: High-time-resolution broadband pump-probe spectroscopy of rhodopsin reveals the loss of reactant and appearance of photoproduct features within ap100 fs, which are signatures of a wavepacket moving through a conical intersection. Experiments are supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

articleTitle: High spatial resolution molecular interferometric imaging study of affinity binding
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have developed molecular interferometric imaging (MI2) for the fundamental study of affinity binding at surfaces, and present high-resolution data of intra-spot molecular kinetics under mass-transport limitations.

articleTitle: All-fiber common-path Fourier-domain optical coherence microscopy for 3D in vivo endoscopic subcellular imaging
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a Fourier-domain all-fiber common-path optical coherence microscopy for 3D in vivo endoscopic subcellular imaging. Image resolution of 2 mumtimes9 mum (transverse times axial) is achieved with nucleus and cell walls clearly visualized.

articleTitle: 2D spectrally encoded confocal microscopy and its application for simultaneous imaging and laser surgery with a single fiber probe
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an endoscope-compatible, mechanical-scan-free microscopy technique and its application as a highly flexible fiber probe which can simultaneously perform imaging and high precision in-situ laser microsurgery.

articleTitle: Laterally intermixed quantum structure for carrier confinement of VCSELs
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Quantum structure intermixing from lateral direction of the mesa sidewall is proposed for VCSELs. I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sub> decrease of 70% and eta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> increase of 75% were achieved by suppression of the surface recombination in the post-type VCSEL.

articleTitle: Laser based synchrotron light sources
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on the generation of synchrotron radiation from laser accelerated relativistic electrons propagating through an undulator. We discuss the necessary steps towards a tuneable, ultrafast, coherent, UV light source.

articleTitle: Probing gas-phase collisional energy transfer with picosecond laser spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Effects of gas-phase collisions on active optical sensing and use of picosecond laser spectroscopy for their characterization are reviewed. Additionally, novel time-resolved approaches to reduce collisional sensitivity and to exploit species-dependent collision rates are discussed.

articleTitle: Integration of 780 and 850-nm vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers into a micro-fluidic microsystem
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate compact integration of 780 and 850-nm vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers into a micro-fluidic microsystem. Absorption at 850 nm and fluorescence pumping at 780 nm of near-infrared fluorescent molecules are presented.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of bottom and top emitting LWIR (8 µm) LED devices
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: For similar GaSb substrate thickness, flip-chip mount bottom emitting LWIR LED device has higher light intensity than top emitting device. Enhanced emission is attributed to better cooling and reflection of light from anode metal surface of the device.

articleTitle: Etching depth dependence of emission properties from InGaN/GaN light emitting diodes with nanohole arrays: Analysis of strain relaxation and surface states
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The effects etching depths of nanohole arrays close to or penetrate the quantum well structures are studied. Our results suggest that when the hole depth is close to the quantum well region, the surface states pinning reduces the band bending and leads to a blue shift of the emission spectrum. When the hole penetrates the quantum well region, similar effects are observed but are due to the strain relaxation in the quantum well.

articleTitle: Polarization-ratio reflectance for determining optical constants using laser high-order harmonics
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a method for deriving optical constants in the extreme ultraviolet from the measured ratio of p- to s-polarized reflectance curves (as a function of angle). These measurements use laser-generated high-order harmonics, which have the advantage of easily rotatable linear polarization. We show that this ratio technique markedly reduces sensitivity to possible systematic brightness and alignment drifts of the harmonic signal during measurement. We also demonstrate that optical constants can be extracted from ratio reflectance measurements as well as they can from absolute reflectance measurements.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic approach of supercontinuum generation in photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that the spectral broadening process inherent to supercontinuum generation may be described as a thermalization process, which results from the natural irreversible evolution of the optical field towards a thermodynamic equilibrium state.

articleTitle: Gain and losses of mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers by frequency chirping spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report an efficient technique to measure gain and losses of quantum cascade lasers (QCLs). It consists on the analysis of the Fabry-Perot fringes induced by the optical injection of a chirped distributed feedback QCL.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Spin Polarization Switching at 2.2 TBit/sec for Proposed Spin-Photon Memory
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: New type of non-volatile high-speed optical memory is proposed, which utilize the magnetization reversal of nanomagnet by spin-polarized photo-excited electrons. To verify high speed of proposed demultiplexing method, the switching of spin polarization at 2.2 TGz was demonstrated.

articleTitle: A multi-resolution approach toward robust fluorescent molecular tomography: Experimental phantom results
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a method to improve depth resolution and accuracy of fluorescent molecular tomography (FMT) by applying a spatial constraint to obtain a low-resolution fluorophore presence map. Results are verified using a CW FMT system.

articleTitle: Modeling the nonlinear add-drop microring filter
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A new model is developed for the effects of the Kerr optical nonlinearity in a microring (racetrack) resonator coupled to input and output waveguides, which takes into account the nonlinearity in the couplers as well as the microring sections, as well as two-photon absorption, in the silicon-on-insulator platform. The switching intensity is 30 dB lower than predicted by existing models which assume the coupler to be linear.

articleTitle: Mode control in large-mode-area fiber lasers via gain filtering
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Gain filtering of higher-order modes in large-mode-area fibers is experimentally demonstrated. While the beam quality degrades with pumping level in conventional fiber lasers, it remains constant in confined-gain fiber lasers due to gain filtering.

articleTitle: Scattering of terahertz radiation from oriented carbon nanotube films
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on the use of terahertz time-domain spectroscopy to measure scattering from multi-walled carbon nanotubes aligned normal to the film plane. Measurements indicate scattering from the nanotubes is significantly stronger than for bulk metal.

articleTitle: The local density of states of metamaterial photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study the local density of states (LDOS) of photonic crystals made with metamaterial inclusions and show that the introduction of metamaterial components substantially widens and deepens band gaps in comparison with normal photonic crystals.

articleTitle: High-harmonic generation in the water window using a CEP-locked few-cycle OPCPA system
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We generated high harmonics using a multi-millijoule few-cycle carrier-envelope-phase-locked optical parametric chirped-pulse amplification (OPCPA) system. We observed the high harmonics in the water window and the carrier-envelope phase (CEP) effect on the harmonic spectra.

articleTitle: Partial cloning of a continuous variable quantum state
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a universal optical amplifier performing near the quantum limit using a four-wave mixing nonlinear interaction. We show that one mode from a bipartite entangled state can be amplified and cloned while maintaining entanglement.

articleTitle: High-power resonantly-diode-pumped CW Er3+:YAG laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using high-brightness laser diodes for resonantly pumping a 1.64 mum Er:YAG laser, 9 W output power is achieved at 64.3% intrinsic slope with up to 95% mode-fill efficiency.

articleTitle: Conditional dynamics in two-mode cavity QED
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The conditional dynamics of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</sup>Rb atoms in a driven two-mode optical cavity shows quantum beats from ground state Larmor precession. We study the manipulation and control of their fringe visibility.

articleTitle: Differential-quadrature-phase-shift (DQPS) quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme named differential-quadrature-phase-shift (DQPS) QKD is presented. A transmitter sends a weak coherent pulse train with a phase of {0, pi} {pi/2. 3pi/2} for each pulse, and a receiver measures it with either one of two delay interferometers respectively having bias phases of 0 and pi/2. The scheme introduces the idea of the BB84 protocol into differential-phase-shift (DPS) QKD, making the system robust against a sequential attack, and may guarantee the unconditional security as in BB84.

articleTitle: Terahertz near-field imaging: Rigorous model for interpreting “antenna approach”
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Classical Mie theory fails to explain high resolution of a terahertz imaging system exploiting scattering of the near-field radiation. Reported numerical model confirms the feasibility of an antenna model which proves the enhanced resolution.

articleTitle: “HVPE InGaN for LEDs- State of the art and horizons”
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We will discuss results of InGaN material and device growth by HVPE. Application of new device concepts for LEDs arising from new HVPE capabilities will be discussed, including all-HVPE InGaN based LEDs for SSL.

articleTitle: Optical spin initialization and nondestructive measurement in a quantum dot molecule
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The spin of an electron in an InAs/GaAs quantum-dot molecule is optically prepared and nondestructively measured through trion-triplet states. With two-laser transmission spectroscopy we demonstrate both simultaneously, something not previously accomplished in single quantum dots.

articleTitle: Semiconductor laser tracking frequency distance gauge
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Space-based astronomical instruments and gravitational experiments require dramatically improved distance measurement accuracy. The Tracking Frequency laser distance Gauge measures to picometer accuracy. We discuss the design of the semiconductor laser version and its controller.

articleTitle: A cavity QED system coupling nitrogen vacancy centers in a diamond nanopillar to a silica microsphere
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A composite cavity QED system, which couples nitrogen vacancy centers in a diamond nanopillar to whispering gallery modes in a silica microsphere and overcomes limitations of earlier diamond nanocrystal based systems, is demonstrated.

articleTitle: GaN-based film-transferred light-emitting diodes with photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Experimental investigation of A-type and B-type guided modes was performed in GaN-based film-transferred photonic crystal light-emitting diodes. Good agreement with the band structure calculated in the limit of two-dimensional free photon was obtained.

articleTitle: Relaxation oscillation suppression in intra-cavity optical parametric oscillators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a passive technique for the suppression of the relaxation oscillations exhibited by optical parametric oscillators pumped internal to laser cavities where gain media with long upper state lifetimes, such as Nd:YAG/YLF/YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, are involved.

articleTitle: Enhanced nonlinear absorption in low-finesse metal-dielectric fabry-perot resonators
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on the nonlinear optical properties of metal-dielectric Fabry-Perot resonators with broad spectral bandwidths in the visible, peak transmittance larger than 70 %, and a nonlinear absorptionup to 20times larger than bulk ZnO.

articleTitle: THz polarimetric components based on metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The interrelation between transmission amplitude and phase spectra of anisotropic metamaterials enables us to develop realistic designs for a terahertz quarter-wave plate and a polarizing terahertz beam splitter based on an anisotropic metamaterial structure.

articleTitle: High-temperature operation of a diode-pumped Nd:YAG laser passively Q-switched by Cr4+:YAG saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The output performances of a Nd:YAG laser passively Q-switched by Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup>:YAG saturable absorber are investigated function of temperature. Small variations in pulse energy and duration were observed over the 25degC to 150degC range.

articleTitle: High-efficiency single-crystal XPW temporal filter for contrast enhancement and pulse shortening
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose an efficient scheme for femtosecond contrast filtering based on cross-polarized wave generation with a super-Gaussian-shaped beam. We reach 50% intensity transmission with a 2.2 time pulse shortening.

articleTitle: GRIN lens and GRIN lens array fabrication with diffusion-driven photopolymer
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce a new method to make gradient index (GRIN) lenses and GRIN lens arrays by exposing diffusion-driven photopolymers using a low-power CW laser. By changing the size and power of the laser beam and the exposure time, the index profile of the GRIN lens can be controlled. A novel feature of this process is that the polymer can be cast on both sides of a micro-optic, followed by exposure and diffusion to develop perfectly aligned lenses.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of spatial quantum correlations in multiple scattering media
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that spatial quantum correlations are induced by multiple scattering of squeezed light. The correlation relates multiple scattered photons at different spatial positions, and is tunable by varying photon fluctuations of the illuminating beam.

articleTitle: Compact femtosecond Nd:phosphate prismless oscillator pumped by a single-mode 150-mW laser diode
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a compact, passively mode-locked and prismless Nd:phosphate laser, pumped by a single-mode, low-power (150-mW) laser diode. We obtained self-starting 270-fs near transform-limited pulses, employing a single Gires-Tournois mirror for intracavity dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Condensation of light in actively mode-locked l1asers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a new approach to active mode-locking (AML) that predicts, under certain conditions, pulse ldquocondensationrdquo, analogous to BEC. In the condensate state, the first AML eigenmode is dominant over all other modes.

articleTitle: Modal and spectral evolution of Raman lines in a H2-filled hollow-core PCF taper
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The spatial mode evolution of spectral Raman components generated in and propagated through a tapered hollow-core PCF reveals adiabatic transition from core modes to surface modes. Its effect on the Raman converter is discussed.

articleTitle: Octave-spanning fiber laser comb with 300 MHz Comb spacing for optical frequency metrology
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A passively mode-locked Er-fiber laser via nonlinear polarization rotation with fundamental repetition rate of 300 MHz is demonstrated. Frequency stabilization of the spectrum-broadened, octave-spanning laser comb and application to optical frequency measurement is reported.

articleTitle: The bandwidth-efficiency product enhancement of GaN based photodiodes by launching a low-temperature-grown recombination center in photo-absorption region
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a GaN-based p-i-n photodiode by inserting a thin low-temperature-grown-GaN layer between p-type Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>N window and intrinsic GaN layer. As compared with control device, our demonstrated one can achieve 3 fold bandwidth-efficiency-products improvement.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable and ultra-wideband wavelength-tunable actively mode-locked short-cavity fiber ring laser using a bismuth-based highly nonlinear erbium-doped fiber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an actively mode-locked short-cavity laser employing a 151 cm-long bismuth-oxide-based highly nonlinear erbium-doped fiber. Stable 10 GHz short pulses are obtained with an 87 nm tuning range. An 8 m-long cavity realizes better stability against external perturbation.

articleTitle: Laser-induced nano-corrugation of a dielectric surface
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that uneven distribution of evanescent field and sub-threshold ablation at a dielectric surface can explain experimentally observed creation of nanometer-sized surface grooves by femtosecond laser pulses.

articleTitle: Shedding light on nutrition
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Supplemental ultraviolet-B radiation (280-320 nm) can increase phenolic compounds in plants and help to preserve them during storage after harvest. The nutritional significance of these compounds and the use of UV-LEDs will be discussed.

articleTitle: Optical control of neural activity by waveguide delivery in genetically targeted brain tissue
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Genetically targeted neurons in brain expressing light sensitive channel Channelrhodopsin can be stimulated optically. We report a novel optical waveguide probe for simultaneous optical stimulation and electrical recording of neurons to modulate neural network behavior.

articleTitle: Sub-200-fs passively mode-locked semiconductor disk laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The femtosecond laser performance of an optically pumped InGaAs-AlGaAs disk laser emitting around 1.04 mum was studied. Using a saturable absorber with a surface-near quantum well, 190-fs-pulses were generated.

articleTitle: Optical-pump THz-probe spectroscopy of P3HT
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We measured the photoconductivity in P3HT excited above and below the band gap using OPTP spectroscopy and extracted values consistent with the intrinsic mobility. We have also investigated the advantages of broadband (> 5 THz) spectroscopy.

articleTitle: High harmonic generation from multiple molecular orbitals
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The contribution of the HOMO and HOMO-1 orbitals are observed in high harmonics from N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. We discuss the harmonic modulation in the rotational revival structure and present a semi-classical model that reproduces the spectral features.

articleTitle: Characterization of soot aggregates based on polarization modulated scattering
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A sensor is demonstrated to characterize soot aggregates based on polarization modulated scattering. Comparison with other techniques shows promising agreement, and extension of the sensor to 1- or 2-dimensional soot imaging is discussed.

articleTitle: Rayleigh-Taylor instability in nonlinear optics
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate, theoretically and experimentally, an all-optical Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Observations of the characteristic spatial period as a function of intensity difference, nonlinearity, and refractive index gradient show excellent agreement with analytical calculations from perturbation theory.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopy of plasmonic fractals
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Transmission properties of subwavelength aperture arrays having deterministic and stochastic fractal morphologies were studied using THz-TDS. We find that transmission enhancement decreases with increasing array size. These observations are explained using density-density correlation function model.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a bottle microresonator
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a very simple technique to fabricate robust micro bottle resonators. Spheroidal WGMs and bottle modes were excited preferentially using a tapered fiber coupled at specific locations along the bottle, and characteristic resonance spectra obtained.

articleTitle: Plasma-enhanced third harmonic generation of ultrafast pulses focused in a gas
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Enhancement of 300times in third harmonic generation conversion efficiency for ultrafast laser pulses in gases is demonstrated. The enhancements are obtained by generating a spatially-localized plasma in the focal region of an ultrashort pulse.

articleTitle: A narrow Rabi frequency window for competition between coherent population trapping and Raman absorption
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the competition mechanism between the coherent population trapping and two-photon Raman absorption in a ladder-type system of cesium cell. When the Rabi frequency of the probe becomes comparable with the effective decay rate, an electromagnetically induced absorption (EIA) dip emerges at the center of the power broadened EIT peak. While the Rabi frequency of the probe exceeds the effective decay rate, a decoherence created by the strong probe field takes place and two-photon Raman absorption dominates the interaction process.

articleTitle: Plasmonic EIT at the Drude damping limit
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a nanoplasmonic analog of electromagnetically induced transparency utilizing a stacked optical metamaterial. Specifically, we achieve a very narrow transparency window with high modulation depth due to nearly complete suppression of radiative losses.

articleTitle: From Type II upconversion to SPDC: A path to broadband polarization entanglement in poled fibers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report type II sum-frequency and second-harmonic generation in a 24-cm-long periodically-poled silica fiber. Quasi-phase matching is achieved for orthogonally-polarized signal and idler over 1520-1575 nm, demonstrating the path to in-fiber broadband polarization-entangled photon pair generation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear polarization rotation in a carbon nanotubes-filled micro-slot fiber device for all-optical wavelength conversion
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate wavelength conversion based on cross-phase modulation induced nonlinear polarization rotation in a carbon nanotubes-filled micro-slot fiber device. Wavelength converted signal with 3-dB power penalty for 10 Gb/s NRZ signal is obtained.

articleTitle: Remote detection of aluminum and trace methane using mobile femtosecond laser system of T&T Lab
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report two remote sensing experiments of aluminum in the winter time and trace methane in the summer time using the mobile femtosecond laser facility T&T (Terawatt & Terahertz) designed by the Defence R&D Canada-Valcartier (DRDC-Valcartier). This system is similar in many respects to Teramobile, the Franco-German laser system. In the first experiment, we demonstrated the feasibility of remote filament-induced breakdown spectroscopy of aluminum targets in an open field in the winter season of Quebec-city when the outside temperature was as low as -20degC. The fluorescence signals are detected in a LIDAR configuration with aluminum target located up to 60 meters. In the second experiment in the summer season, we remotely detected trace methane in the open field during daytime (with strong sun light) up to 20 meters.

articleTitle: Beam shaping in quantum cascade ring lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Mid-infrared beam shaping is demonstrated by using grating coupled surface emitting quantum cascade ring lasers. The devices allow for far-field tuning, ranging from highly symmetric spot- to ring-shaped beam patterns, depending on the grating period.

articleTitle: Optomechanically tunable photonic crystals for cavity QED
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A new cavity-optomechanical system has been developed comprised of two doubly-clamped silicon nitride cantilevers with a 1D photonic crystal etched into them. We will discuss the optical properties of the system and potential applications to solid-state cavity QED with diamond color centers.

articleTitle: Optical fiber refractometer with improved sensitivity based on an offset tilted fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Highly sensitive fiber-optic refractometer with an over-offset tilted fiber Bragg grating configuration is proposed based on strong cladding-core recoupling. Reflection with two well-defined bands performs an improved refractive index measurement combining with power self-calibration property.

articleTitle: Effect of structural distortion on fabry-perot temperature response
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Low expansion glass cavities with optically contacted mirrors can exhibit structural distortions at the mirrors which significantly shift the temperature at which dv/dT=0. An analytical analysis that incorporates finite element modeling is given.

articleTitle: High efficient and tunable edge emitting microlaser on photonic crystal slab
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Tunable edge emitting microlaser was realized with a line defect waveguide, in which the radii of holes adjacent to the defect was varied gradually. A tunable range of 17 nm was obtained experimentally.

articleTitle: Comparison of R-dependent ionization and bond-softening as mechanisms for creating vibrational coherence in hot molecules
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We compare wavepackets induced by ldquoR-dependent ionizationrdquo and bond-softening in strong fields through both simulations and experiments. We conclude that the former produces stronger vibrations in hot molecules than the latter and results in vibrational cooling.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional super-resolution single-molecule fluorescence imaging using a double-helix point spread function
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Fluorescence imaging with resolution ten times better than the diffraction limit in three dimensions over a depth of field of 2 mum is demonstrated with a widefield microscope that exhibits a double-helix point spread function.

articleTitle: Negative differential resistance and pulse instabilities in minimalized quantum cascade laser structures
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study high performing mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers with highly discretized injector regions. We observe negative differential resistance features of ~2V that persist to room temperature and pulse instabilities below 180K.

articleTitle: Experimental observation of a microscopic cascaded contribution to the fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the first, to the best of our knowledge, experiment on the separation of the microscopic cascaded contribution to the fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility, which comes from the third-order microscopic hyperpolarizability.

articleTitle: High order harmonic generation driven by an Yb-doped fiber amplifier system at 1 MHz repetition rate
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate high brightness XUV emission through high order harmonic generation driven by a 100 muJ-class ytterbium-doped fiber, CPA system at controllable ultrahigh (100 kHz to 1 MHz) repetition rate.

articleTitle: Large enhancement in TEM00 solar laser power by a light guide assembly-elliptical cavity
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Through a fused silica light guide assembly, the concentrated solar radiation is efficiently focused into a small diameter Nd:YAG rod by a sharp elliptical cavity. TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</sub> laser power is triple that of the 2D-DCPC cavity.

articleTitle: Direct phase-sensitive impulsive vibrational spectroscopy with spectral interferometry
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: New techniques for time-domain ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy through direct time-dependent phase detection of coherently excited vibrations via spectral interferometry. Three variants with advantages for spectral resolution, sensitivity and speed are presented.

articleTitle: 24 W 888 nm pumped Nd:YVO4 1342 nm oscillator operating in the TEM00 mode
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on a 888 nm diode pumped Nd:YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> cw-laser at 1342 nm, which provides an output power of 24 W into a diffraction limited beam. An optical conversion efficiency of 29 % was obtained.

articleTitle: Unusual quantum correlations and photon antibunching in an off-resonant quantum dot photonic-crystal cavity system
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce a medium-dependent master equation formalism to study the off-resonant coupling behavior between a single quantum dot and a photonic-crystal cavity. Several surprising effects are found that help explain recent experiments.

articleTitle: Electrically tunable metamaterial for polarization-independent terahertz modulation
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a polarization-insensitive, electrically tunable metamaterial operating at terahertz (THz) frequencies and demonstrate the fast modulation of a propagating THz wave. The structure is composed of gold crosses on n-doped gallium arsenide (GaAs).

articleTitle: Interaction of intense narrowband THz pulses with coherent excitons in semiconductor QWs
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the coherent dynamics of excitonic wavepackets in semiconductors driven by intense narrowband THz pulses. Time-resolved THz-pump and optical-probe measurements demonstrate strong nonlinear-optical transients of the light-hole and heavy-hole excitonic resonances in GaAs/AlGaAs QWs.

articleTitle: Anomalously high refractive index of an array of vertically aligned gold nanopillars on silicon
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Reflectivity measurements on a film consisting of gold nanopillars surrounded by an anodized aluminum oxide medium suggest a refractive index much larger than that predicted by considering the dispersion curves of gold and aluminum oxide.

articleTitle: Demonstrations of an air-slot photonic crystal nanocavity with ultrasmall mode volumes for enhanced light-matter interactions
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally a photonic crystal nanocavity with an ultrasmall modal volume of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>(lambda/n)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, based on a designed air-slot in a two-dimensional photonic crystal lattice. Coupling to the tightly localized nanocavity of the fabricated sample is achieved with the tapered fiber, with strong applications to nonlinear optics and cavity quantum electrodynamics studies.

articleTitle: Challenges and opportunities for next generation diode laser active sensing
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Near-IR diode laser sensors have successfully entered a number of commercial markets. New application opportunities for these and related sensors in the automotive industry are described. Progress in MWIR and LWIR diode laser-based sources is highlighted, along with new opportunities that these lasers will address. Heterodyne measurement techniques, allowing for sensitive room-temperature detection methods in the FIR are described.

articleTitle: Resolution, contrast, and noise of quantum and thermal ghost images
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We compare the quality of images formed by quantum and thermal ghost imaging systems. We find the resolution to be the same and determine the scaling laws for the contrast and signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Scaling of average power of coherent terahertz pulses by stacking GaAs wafers
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The average terahertz output power generated from stacked GaAs wafers using two CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> lasers is scaled up by 160. The highest average output power is measured to be 29.8 muW by stacking ten wafers.

articleTitle: Laser induced tunneling in less than 12 attoseconds: Instantaneous or invalid concept?
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We use attosecond angular streaking to place an intensity-averaged upper limit of 12 attoseconds on the tunneling delay time in strong field ionization of helium. This is far shorter than most tunneling times discussed before.

articleTitle: High-pulse-energy optical parametric oscillator in the near- and mid-infrared
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report an extended-cavity femtosecond optical parametric oscillator, based on MgO:PPLN and synchronously pumped by a commercial Yb:fibre laser. Preliminary results show 15 MHz-repetition-frequency, 475 fs-duration pulses at 1.5 mum, with energies of 36 nJ.

articleTitle: Mode selection in a microdisk laser coupled to a passive cavity for optical interconnections
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Coupling a microdisk based laser to an external passive cavity can be used to strengthen mode selectivity and get a single, unidirectional and tunable output waveguide.

articleTitle: Super-resolution imaging using spatial fourier transform infrared spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a scheme for far-field subwavelength spectroscopy and imaging in the mid-IR and THz bands. This approach is based on scattering from an acoustic grating and can recover both the amplitude and the phase of the incident field.

articleTitle: Effective indicators for oral cancer diagnosis based on optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A swept-source optical coherence tomography system is used to clinically scan oral precancer and cancer patients for statistically analyzing the effective indicators of diagnosis including the signal standard deviation, spatial-frequency spectral shape, and epithelium thickness.

articleTitle: Temporally resolved characterization of iron nanoparticles using a time-resolved laser technique
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: For the first time, time-resolved laser-induced incandescence (TiRe-LII) has been used to investigate the metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) process of iron in a fluidized bed reactor characterizing nanoparticles deposited on a substrate surface.

articleTitle: Photon logic gates using ultraslow light
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Photon logic gates are observed using ultraslow light. The building block of the photon logic gate is photon routing phenomenon, where the routing is based on atomic coherence enhanced by ultraslow light.

articleTitle: Dynamic light-matter coupling across multiple spatial dimensions in a quantum dots-in-a-well heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Ultrafast density-dependent optical spectroscopic measurements on a quantum dots-in-a-well heterostructure reveal several distinctive phenomena, most notably a strong coupling between the quantum well population and light absorption at the quantum dot excited state.

articleTitle: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dot whispering-gallery microlaser — a comparative study of two approaches
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The microlaser consists of a tapered-fiber-coupled fused-silica microsphere, with HgTe nanocrystals deposited on one tapered fiber. Compared to a microlaser having a coated microsphere, the lasing signal is cleaner and the cavity Q remains high.

articleTitle: Statistical light-mode dynamics of passive mode-locking with slow saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We employ a novel dynamical approach to study the slow saturable absorber mode-locking with noise. We obtain explicit expressions for the condition of pulse existence and continuum stability, the pulse power and the minimal pulse width, and present the guidelines for optimal system configuration.

articleTitle: 1.3 Watt Single-Frequency Nd:YLF/ppKTP red laser
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using a temperature-tuned ppKTP crystal, a record 1.3 W single-frequency red laser at 661 nm is achieved from intra-cavity second-harmonic generation of a Nd:YLiF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ring laser oscillating on the pi-polarized transition (lambda~1321 nm).

articleTitle: 1.55-µm VCSEL arrays for optical multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a monolithically integrated, individually addressable 2D VCSEL array of five lasers which can be coupled into the core of a multi-mode fiber. This device, emitting at 1.55 mum with a perchannel modulation bandwidth in excess of 10 GHz, is especially designed for optical multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) data transmission.

articleTitle: 16 Chip, 18 Gchips/s Walsh-Code implementation of an ECDMA access network using two time-shifted FIR filters
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time an electronically processed Walsh Code with 16 chips at 18 Gchip/s. An auto-cross correlation ratio of 18.1 dB is achieved between two orthogonal codes after transmission over 10 km of SMF.

articleTitle: Effect of water impurity in CsLiB6O10 crystals on UV optical properties
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigated the effect of water impurity in a CsLiB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> (CLBO) crystal on the ultraviolet (UV) properties of the bulk laser-induced damage threshold (LIDT). The water impurity was eliminated by heating the CLBO sample with dimensions of 5 times 5 times 10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 150degC in ambient atmosphere and subsequently in dry atmosphere. The bulk LIDT of the sample after the heat treatment improved by about 1.6-fold compared with that before the heat treatment.

articleTitle: Two-photon spectroscopy of InAs quantum dot molecules
publicationTitle: 2009 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2009 Conference on Quantum electronics and Laser Science Conference
